vignette: Patient D is a 40-year-old woman with a history of migraines who presents to the emergency room complaining of a new and severe headache. The pain started 8 hours ago toward a routine shopping trip. Patient D describes it as one of the worst headaches of her life, and states that it was preceded by a visual aura and gradually progressed from unilateral to holo-cranial pain. Patient D also describes photosensitivity and prefers to keep her eyes closed. Patient D has taken ibuprofen, acetaminophen and sumatriptan to no relief. The patient is still in agony and now asks if you can give her something to make the pain go away. The patient appears calm and composed.
rationale: Severe migraine refractory to abortive meds; opioid analgesia appropriate.
